title: Looking for feedback on the art, effects, and scene composition of my first sci-fi game
author: ralphhhhhy
selftext:
Hi everyone! I'm working on a top-down sci-fi game in Godot. This short clip shows some ship movement, combat, damage, and destruction. I'd like to get some outside feedback on how it looks and hear from people working through similar production challenges.



AI tools are a big part of the workflow. Here's roughly what I'm using:



\- \*\*Codex:\*\* programming, development tools, and implementing and iterating on things in the engine.

\- \*\*Godot:\*\* the game engine, rendering, and real-time VFX using particles and shaders.

\- \*\*Image 2 / 2.5:\*\* visual exploration, 2D ship art, and references for materials and textures.

\- \*\*Tripo:\*\* generating 3D assets and textures from visual references.

\- \*\*Blender:\*\* modeling, mesh cleanup, material work, UVs, baking, and preparing assets for the game.



I've managed to get some art results I'm happy with using AI, but polishing them into something consistent in-game still takes a lot of time. Matching the style, adjusting materials, and checking how everything reads at gameplay scale have involved a lot of back and forth.



I'd particularly appreciate feedback on:



1. \*\*Art and visual consistency.\*\* What's your first impression? Do the ships and environment feel like they belong together? What looks distracting or out of place? If you've used AI in an art workflow, what has helped you get consistent results with less time spent on cleanup and revisions?



2. \*\*VFX, sound effects, and music.\*\* Do you have tools, asset libraries, tutorials, or workflows you'd recommend for thrusters, weapon impacts, explosions, and sci-fi audio? I'm also looking for a practical way to approach background music. AI and conventional approaches are both welcome. I'm interested in what gives you enough control to make the results fit the game.



3. \*\*Scene composition.\*\* How would you approach arranging large structures, rocks, and debris in a scene like this? I'm trying to give it a sense of depth and scale while keeping the ships readable. What helps a space scene feel deliberately composed, with a good balance between empty space and detail?



No need to answer everything—even a specific observation about one moment in the clip would help. I'd also be interested in seeing examples of workflows that have worked for you.



(English isn't my first language, so I used GPT to help polish the wording of this post.)

comments.author: BanjoThunderbird
comments.body: Love the look of the background and how the parallax works, but the actual foreground ships don't match the aesthetic. The background has a really nice sort of minimal-realistic sci-fi look, but the foreground ships have a retro pixel art look.

replies.author: ralphhhhhy
replies.body: The spaceship was originally made using hard-edged sci-fi anime style. Later, to give the background a sense of depth, I used a 3D approach and some 3D-to-2D techniques. I guess the inconsistency is probably because the spaceship is actually 2D. I’ll try using a 3D model, thanks.
